findings.title: Key sections only exist as #fragments
findings.excerpt: 11 sections at #fragments of the home page (#all, #myownsession, #myownedu, #myownteach, #myownarc, #myownmenu, ...), against 4 other pages with an address of their own
findings.description: Each part of your offer lives at a #section of one page rather than at its own URL. Search engines ignore everything after #, so one URL can only rank once: none of these sections can be the page that answers a search for it, and an AI can't cite or link one.
findings.fix_prompt: My site keeps 11 sections at #fragments of the home page (#all, #myownsession, #myownedu, #myownteach, #myownarc, #myownmenu, ...), against 4 other pages with an address of their own. Give each important section its own page with its own URL, <title>, meta description and H1 (for example /products/name), keep a short summary on the home page linking to it, and add the new pages to the sitemap.
findings.verify: Each section should have its own address you can paste into Google's URL Inspection, and appear in /sitemap.xml.

findings.title: No canonical URL
findings.description: A canonical tag tells search engines which address is the real one when a page is reachable several ways (with and without www, a trailing slash, tracking parameters). Without it they guess, and can split your ranking between copies.
findings.fix_prompt: Add <link rel="canonical" href="..."> to the <head> of every page, pointing at that page's own full URL on my main domain (/brand). Generate it from the route so each page gets its own.
findings.verify: View source on each page and check the canonical is the page's own address.

findings.title: Meta descriptions too short or too long
findings.description: Search results show about 160 characters. A longer description is cut off mid-sentence; a very short one wastes the space.
findings.fix_prompt: Rewrite these meta descriptions to 70 to 160 characters: /: 217 characters; /open: 161 characters.

findings.title: Same sites linked with and without www
findings.excerpt: myownlingo.com: myownlingo.com in page links; www.myownlingo.com in llms.txt and structured data (the site serves www.myownlingo.com); myowntrader.com: myowntrader.com in page links; www.myowntrader.com in llms.txt and structured data (the site serves www.myowntrader.com)
findings.description: You link to the same sites by two different addresses (with and without www) in different places. One of each pair redirects, and to a crawler or an AI reading your llms.txt they look like separate sites.
findings.fix_prompt: I link to these sites with both www and bare addresses: myownlingo.com: myownlingo.com in page links; www.myownlingo.com in llms.txt and structured data (the site serves www.myownlingo.com); myowntrader.com: myowntrader.com in page links; www.myowntrader.com in llms.txt and structured data (the site serves www.myowntrader.com). Use the form each site actually serves (the one it doesn't redirect away from) everywhere: page links, llms.txt and structured data.
findings.verify: Search your source for each domain and check every mention uses the same form.

findings.title: Internal links that redirect
findings.description: Links between your own pages go to an address that redirects. Every one costs a crawler an extra request and some of the link's value.
findings.fix_prompt: My site links to its own pages at addresses that redirect: /brand/ -> /brand. Change those links to the final address (usually a trailing slash or the www/bare form).
findings.verify: Re-run this scan; the links should no longer be listed.

findings.title: Products without prices in the structured data
findings.excerpt: MyOwnSession; MyOwnEdu; MyOwnTeach; MyOwnArc; MyOwnMenu; MyOwnLingo; MyOwnTrader; MyOwnReach; and 2 more
findings.description: Your structured data lists products or apps without an Offer, so the price you show on the page isn't machine-readable. AI assistants comparing prices will look elsewhere, or guess.
findings.fix_prompt: My JSON-LD lists these without an Offer: MyOwnSession; MyOwnEdu; MyOwnTeach; MyOwnArc; MyOwnMenu; MyOwnLingo; MyOwnTrader; MyOwnReach; and 2 more. Add an 'offers' to each: {"@type": "Offer", "price": "15", "priceCurrency": "GBP"}, or an AggregateOffer with lowPrice and highPrice when there are several plans. Use the prices shown on the page.
findings.verify: Paste the page into Google's Rich Results Test and check each product shows its price.

findings.title: Link previews are incomplete
findings.description: Open Graph and Twitter tags decide what a shared link looks like on LinkedIn, Slack, X, WhatsApp and iMessage. Missing ones give a bare URL with no picture.
findings.fix_prompt: These pages are missing link-preview tags: /brand: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, twitter:card. Add them to each page's <head>: og:title, og:description, og:url (the page's own full URL), og:image (a full URL to a 1200x630 image) and twitter:card set to summary_large_image. Generate them from the same title and description the page already uses.
findings.verify: Paste the URL into opengraph.xyz or LinkedIn's Post Inspector.

findings.title: Organization schema is missing fields
findings.description: Your Organization structured data is missing sameAs. sameAs (links to your profiles elsewhere) is how search engines and AI connect your site to the rest of your presence.
findings.fix_prompt: My Organization JSON-LD is missing sameAs. Add them: name, url, logo (full image URL) and sameAs as an array of full URLs to my profiles (LinkedIn, X, GitHub, Product Hunt, Crunchbase). Only list profiles that exist.
findings.verify: Paste the page into validator.schema.org and check the fields appear.

findings.title: Pages missing from the sitemap
findings.excerpt: sitemap lists 4 URLs; the crawl found 5 pages. Not listed: /brand
findings.description: Your site links to pages your sitemap doesn't list. Crawlers can still find them by following links, but the sitemap is your statement of what matters, and pages left out of it get crawled less often.
findings.fix_prompt: My sitemap.xml is missing pages my site links to (sitemap lists 4 URLs; the crawl found 5 pages. Not listed: /brand). Generate the sitemap from my routes rather than by hand, so every public page is listed, and leave out only pages that shouldn't be found (admin, thank-you pages).
findings.verify: Open /sitemap.xml and check each page your navigation links to is listed.

findings.title: Sitemap dates are older than the pages
findings.excerpt: /: lastmod 2026-09-28, but the page mentions 13 October 2026
findings.description: Your sitemap says these pages last changed earlier than the server says they did. Crawlers use lastmod to decide what to re-read, so an old date means your changes are picked up late, or a wrong date teaches them to ignore it.
findings.fix_prompt: The <lastmod> dates in my sitemap.xml are older than my pages (/: lastmod 2026-09-28, but the page mentions 13 October 2026). Set each page's lastmod from when its content last changed (the file's git commit date or the record's updated_at), not a fixed date, and regenerate the sitemap on every deploy.
findings.verify: Open /sitemap.xml after your next content change and check that page's lastmod moved.
